_meta.note: Breed reference for LUVD. Scores are 1-5 general breed tendencies, NOT claims about an individual dog. energy: 1=couch potato, 5=needs a job. apartment: 1=poor fit, 5=great fit. experience: 1=great first dog, 5=needs an experienced owner. alone: 1=needs company most of the day, 5=comfortable through a workday. adult_lbs: typical adult weight range, used to project growth and scale food cost.
_meta.source: General breed-typical guidance. Always defer to the rescue's own assessment of the individual animal.

_default.temperament: Every dog is an individual — temperament depends far more on this dog's history and personality than on breed. The rescue's write-up is the best guide.
_default.exercise: Most adult dogs do well with 30-60 minutes of walking a day plus play and sniffing time.
_default.grooming: Brush regularly, bathe as needed, keep nails trimmed and ears clean.
_default.nyc: Ask the rescue about leash manners, elevator and stair comfort, alone-time tolerance, and whether the dog settles in a small space.

mixed breed.temperament: Mixed-breed dogs pull traits from several lines, which often means fewer breed-linked health problems and a temperament best judged by meeting the dog. What the foster or shelter observed day to day is far more predictive than any breed guess.
mixed breed.exercise: Depends on the individual. A daily walk plus play is the baseline; ask the foster how the dog behaves after a quiet day.
mixed breed.grooming: Varies with coat type. Short coats need little; longer or double coats need regular brushing.
mixed breed.nyc: Mixes are often excellent city dogs. Building breed restrictions are usually enforced on what a dog looks like, so ask the rescue how the dog is typically identified.

labrador retriever.temperament: Friendly, people-focused and famously food-motivated, which makes training straightforward. Labs stay adolescent longer than many breeds and are often goofy well past their second birthday.
labrador retriever.exercise: High needs — 60-90 minutes daily. Labs love retrieving and swimming, and an under-exercised Lab tends to get mouthy and destructive.
labrador retriever.grooming: Short double coat that sheds heavily year-round and more in spring and fall. Weekly brushing helps a lot.
labrador retriever.nyc: Can do well in an apartment if genuinely exercised. Size and shedding are the main constraints; most are elevator- and crowd-tolerant.

golden retriever.temperament: Gentle, eager to please and highly social. Goldens generally love strangers, children and other dogs, and dislike being left alone for long stretches.
golden retriever.exercise: 60-90 minutes daily plus mental work. They thrive on fetch and training games.
golden retriever.grooming: Long double coat needs brushing several times a week and sheds a lot.
golden retriever.nyc: Manageable in a city if exercised well. Their sociability suits busy sidewalks and dog runs.

poodle.temperament: Genuinely one of the smartest breeds — quick to learn, and quick to invent bad habits if bored. Poodles are sensitive, bond hard to their people and tend to be more reserved with strangers than retrievers.
poodle.exercise: 45-60 minutes daily plus puzzle work. Mental exercise matters as much as physical for this breed.
poodle.grooming: High maintenance. The curly single coat doesn't shed much but mats easily; expect brushing several times a week and professional grooming every 6-8 weeks.
poodle.nyc: Excellent city dogs — low shedding, adaptable and highly trainable. Budget for grooming.

doberman pinscher.temperament: Intelligent, intensely loyal and strongly bonded to their person — Dobermans are often described as velcro dogs. They are naturally alert and watchful, which needs to be channeled through early socialization rather than suppressed.
doberman pinscher.exercise: High — 60-90 minutes daily plus training. A bored Doberman is an anxious Doberman.
doberman pinscher.grooming: Very easy. Short coat, weekly wipe-down, minimal shedding. They feel the cold and often need a coat in a NYC winter.
doberman pinscher.nyc: Their size and reputation trigger breed restrictions in many buildings — check your lease before falling in love. Otherwise they are clean, quiet indoors and settle well.

german shepherd.temperament: Confident, highly trainable and deeply loyal, bred to work all day alongside a handler. They are naturally aloof with strangers and need thorough socialization to be comfortable in a crowded city.
german shepherd.exercise: High — 60-90+ minutes daily plus a job to do. Scent work and obedience are ideal outlets.
german shepherd.grooming: Heavy double-coat shedding year-round with two big blowouts a year. Brush several times a week.
german shepherd.nyc: Demanding in an apartment: large, vocal and often reactive to the constant stimulus of a city street. Very doable for an experienced owner, hard for a first-timer.

siberian husky.temperament: Independent, playful and famously stubborn. Huskies were bred to run for hours and are generally friendly with everyone — they make poor guard dogs and excellent escape artists.
siberian husky.exercise: Very high — 90+ minutes of real exertion daily. Under-exercised huskies dig, howl and escape.
siberian husky.grooming: Thick double coat that sheds enormously twice a year. Frequent brushing is not optional.
siberian husky.nyc: One of the harder city breeds: vocal, high-energy, heat-sensitive and rarely reliable off leash. Needs an owner ready to run in the cold.

french bulldog.temperament: Comic, affectionate and people-oriented. Frenchies want to be with you constantly and are usually easygoing with strangers and other dogs.
french bulldog.exercise: Low — two or three short walks and some indoor play. They tire quickly.
french bulldog.grooming: Short coat is easy, but facial folds need regular cleaning to prevent infection.
french bulldog.nyc: Near-ideal apartment dog: small, quiet and low-exercise. The serious caveat is breathing — flat faces make them dangerously heat-intolerant, so summer walks must be early, short and shaded. Expect higher vet costs.

bulldog.temperament: Calm, stubborn and affectionate. Bulldogs are famously low-drive and content to spend most of the day asleep near you.
bulldog.exercise: Low — short walks only, and never in the heat.
bulldog.grooming: Short coat, but skin and facial folds need regular cleaning.
bulldog.nyc: Quiet and space-efficient. Same heat and breathing cautions as the French Bulldog; plan for higher vet bills.

american pit bull terrier.temperament: Affectionate, people-loving and often startlingly goofy — pit bull type dogs are typically very social with humans. Dog-to-dog tolerance varies a lot by individual, so the rescue's observations matter more than the label.
american pit bull terrier.exercise: High — 60+ minutes daily plus chew and puzzle outlets. They are strong and benefit from structured training.
american pit bull terrier.grooming: Very easy. Short coat, minimal shedding, thin coat means a winter jacket.
american pit bull terrier.nyc: The main obstacle is paperwork, not the dog: many buildings and insurers restrict pit bull type dogs, and enforcement is based on appearance. Confirm your building's policy first.

american staffordshire terrier.temperament: Confident, loyal and very people-focused, with the same goofy streak as other bully breeds. Strong-willed but highly food-motivated and responsive to reward-based training.
american staffordshire terrier.exercise: High — 60+ minutes daily plus mental work.
american staffordshire terrier.grooming: Minimal. Short coat, occasional brushing, needs a coat in winter.
american staffordshire terrier.nyc: Frequently caught by building breed restrictions. Check your lease. Otherwise a clean, adaptable and affectionate city dog.

terrier.temperament: Bold, curious and busy. Terriers were bred to hunt independently, which shows up as tenacity, a strong prey drive and a low tolerance for boredom. They are often more dog-selective than people-selective.
terrier.exercise: Moderate to high, and mental more than physical — 45-60 minutes plus digging, sniffing or puzzle outlets.
terrier.grooming: Varies. Wiry coats need hand-stripping or clipping every few months; smooth coats need very little.
terrier.nyc: Their small size suits apartments well. Watch for barking at hallway noise and a strong interest in squirrels and rats.

chihuahua.temperament: Bold and deeply bonded to one or two people. Chihuahuas are often wary of strangers and can be snappy if they were never taught that hands are safe — early gentle socialization matters.
chihuahua.exercise: Low — short walks and indoor play are plenty.
chihuahua.grooming: Easy for both smooth and long coats. Dental care is the real priority; small breeds are prone to tooth disease.
chihuahua.nyc: Extremely apartment-friendly and easy to carry on the subway. They get cold fast and need a sweater most of the winter.

pomeranian.temperament: Lively, bold and much bigger in attitude than in body. Poms are alert little dogs who tend to announce everything that happens in the hallway.
pomeranian.exercise: Low to moderate — a couple of short walks plus play.
pomeranian.grooming: Thick double coat needs brushing several times a week to avoid mats.
pomeranian.nyc: Great size for a small apartment, but barking is the thing to work on early if you share walls.

great pyrenees.temperament: Calm, independent and gentle, bred to guard livestock alone for days. That independence means they think for themselves rather than looking to you for direction, and they are natural night barkers.
great pyrenees.exercise: Low to moderate for their size — a couple of long relaxed walks. They are not endurance athletes.
great pyrenees.grooming: Enormous double coat that sheds constantly. Brush several times a week.
great pyrenees.nyc: Hard in an apartment mostly because of size, shedding and their instinct to bark at every noise. Individuals raised as city dogs can do fine — ask the foster.

cattle dog.temperament: Whip-smart, intense and endlessly driven. Australian Cattle Dogs bond hard to one person and need work; without it they herd whatever is available, including people and bikes.
cattle dog.exercise: Very high — 90+ minutes plus daily training or a dog sport.
cattle dog.grooming: Short weather-resistant double coat, easy but sheds seasonally.
cattle dog.nyc: One of the toughest apartment breeds. Only realistic if you are genuinely active and ready to train daily.

shepherd.temperament: Herding-type dogs are typically bright, biddable and attentive to their person, with a tendency to be watchful and sometimes reactive to fast movement.
shepherd.grooming: Usually a double coat with regular shedding; brush weekly or more.
shepherd.nyc: Trainability helps a lot in the city. Socialize early to bikes, scooters and crowds.

retriever.temperament: Retriever types are generally sociable, food-motivated and easy to train — among the most forgiving dogs for a first-time owner.
retriever.exercise: High — 60-90 minutes daily with fetch and swimming as favorites.
retriever.grooming: Double coats that shed; brush weekly.
retriever.nyc: Size and shedding are the constraints, temperament rarely is.

feist.temperament: A small Southern hunting type — quick, alert, affectionate with their people and very driven by scent and movement. Think terrier energy in a compact frame.
feist.exercise: Moderate to high — 45-60 minutes plus sniffing and chase games.
feist.nyc: Good size for an apartment, but the prey drive is real on a city street full of pigeons and rats.

beagle.temperament: Cheerful, sociable and governed almost entirely by their nose. Beagles are friendly with nearly everyone and famously hard to recall once they catch a scent.
beagle.exercise: Moderate — 45-60 minutes with plenty of sniffing.
beagle.nyc: Good size for an apartment; the baying voice is the thing to check with neighbors.

dachshund.temperament: Bold, comic and stubborn, bred to go down a badger hole alone. Devoted to their people and often quite vocal.
dachshund.exercise: Low to moderate — walks on flat ground and gentle play.
dachshund.grooming: Depends on coat; smooth is easy, long and wire need brushing.
dachshund.nyc: Great apartment size. Protect the back — discourage stair and furniture jumping, and use a harness rather than a collar.

shih tzu.temperament: Bred purely for companionship — affectionate, cheerful and content to be near you all day.
shih tzu.exercise: Low — short walks and indoor play.
shih tzu.grooming: High. The long coat mats quickly; either commit to daily brushing or keep it in a short puppy cut.
shih tzu.nyc: An easy, quiet apartment companion. Flat-faced, so keep summer walks short and cool.

border collie.temperament: Widely considered the most intelligent breed, and that is a demand rather than a convenience. Border Collies need a job and will invent one — often herding people or chasing traffic — if you don't supply it.
border collie.exercise: Very high — 90+ minutes plus daily mental work or a dog sport.
border collie.grooming: Medium double coat, brush a few times a week.
border collie.nyc: A difficult apartment fit unless you are committed to serious daily activity.

boxer.temperament: Playful, exuberant and deeply attached to their families. Boxers stay puppyish for years and are usually great with children.
boxer.nyc: Doable with real exercise. Flat-faced enough to be heat-sensitive, and they get cold in winter.

maltese.temperament: Gentle, affectionate lap dogs who bond closely and prefer not to be left alone for long.
maltese.grooming: High. The silky white coat mats and stains without frequent brushing.
maltese.nyc: Excellent small-apartment companion. Watch for separation anxiety and hallway barking.

yorkshire terrier.temperament: Confident and lively, with more terrier boldness than their size suggests. Strongly bonded to their person.
yorkshire terrier.exercise: Low to moderate — short walks plus play.
yorkshire terrier.grooming: High if kept long; much easier in a short cut. Dental care matters.
yorkshire terrier.nyc: Very apartment-friendly. Barking at hallway noise is the common complaint.

husky mix.temperament: Husky mixes usually keep some of the vocal, independent, high-energy character, softened by whatever else is in the mix.
husky mix.grooming: Usually a shedding double coat; brush often.
husky mix.nyc: Ask the foster specifically about howling and alone-time — that is the usual apartment dealbreaker.
